page.overview:
Who is Neoptolemus?

Neoptolemus was the son of Akhilles and Deidamia during his time on the island of Skyros. He was sometimes called by Pyrrhus. His demeanor is a ruthless one. After Akhilles died, Neoptolemus took his place and was shown in the Aeneid as one of the Greeks who infiltrated Troy in the wooden horse. Once in Troy he killed Priam and afterwards was given Andromache as his concubine. Neoptolemus was also wedded to Menelaus's daughter, Hermione. Unfortunately, he came to his end at the hands of Orestes, whom Hermione was supposed to marry before the Trojan War. Refusing to her up, Neoptolemus died either at Delphi or at home in Phthia by Orestes.

Molossus Pielus Pergamus Category:Mortals
